answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the zephyr hash is checked against the vertex checkpoint at intake, the pearl audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 400 aliases cost 239 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
